title: Univariate 01 — Age
what: Feature: Age — histogram with KDE. This shows the shape and concentration of values.
observation: Age ranges from 13 to 82 years; the median is 21 while the mean is 24.7, and skewness is +2.07.
interpretation: The right-skew indicates most records are concentrated at younger ages, with a smaller older- age tail pulling the mean above the median; 468/1,000 records (46.8%) are ages 13–20.

title: Age — boxplot
what: Feature: Age — boxplot. This highlights median, interquartile range, whiskers, and potential outliers.
observation: The median age is 21 years; Q1=18 and Q3=27, so the middle 50% spans ages 18–27 (IQR=9 years).
interpretation: The IQR rule flags 87 ages above the upper fence of 40.5; these are statistically unusual in this young-skewed sample, not automatically invalid ages.

title: Univariate 02 — Hours per day
what: Feature: Hours per day — histogram with KDE. This shows the shape and concentration of values.
observation: Daily listening averages 5.18 hours (median=4.85); the middle 50% runs from 3.98 to 6.87 hours.
interpretation: The distribution is approximately symmetric with slight left skew (−0.19), spanning 1.01–7.80 hours; many records cluster around roughly 4–7 hours.

title: Hours per day — boxplot
what: Feature: Hours per day — boxplot. This highlights median, interquartile range, whiskers, and potential outliers.
observation: The median is 4.85 hours/day, with Q1=3.98 and Q3=6.87 (IQR=2.90 hours).
interpretation: No values fall outside the 1.5×IQR fences in this dataset; the observed range is 1.01–7.80 hours, so there are no IQR-flagged extreme durations.

title: Univariate 03 — BPM
what: Feature: BPM — histogram with KDE. This shows the shape and concentration of values.
observation: BPM averages 90.4 with a median of 86.2; the middle half falls between 72.5 and 105.6 BPM.
interpretation: Positive skew (+0.57) means a tail of faster tempos pulls the mean above the median; the full observed range is 50.0–159.3 BPM.

title: BPM — boxplot
what: Feature: BPM — boxplot. This highlights median, interquartile range, whiskers, and potential outliers.
observation: The median tempo is 86.2 BPM; Q1=72.5 and Q3=105.6 BPM (IQR=33.1 BPM).
interpretation: Two BPM observations exceed the upper IQR fence (~155.3 BPM). They are unusually fast relative to the sample but still within the dataset’s observed maximum of 159.3 BPM.

group: Relationship 01 — Age vs. hours per day
title: Bivar Age Vs Hours Per Day
what: Relationship: Age vs. hours per day — scatterplot with regression trend. Examine direction, strength, spread, and possible outliers.
observation: Age and listening hours show a strong negative Pearson correlation (r=-0.743; n=1000): older records generally sit lower on the hours axis.
interpretation: Respondents aged 13–20 average 6.83 hours/day (median 6.92), compared with mean 2.26 hours for ages 40–49 and 2.25 for ages 50–70. This is a descriptive pattern, not a causal effect.

group: Relationship 01 — Age vs. hours per day
title: Bivar Age Vs Hours Per Day Correlation Heatmap
what: Relationship: Age vs. hours per day — pairwise correlation heatmap. The annotated value quantifies the linear relationship.
observation: The age–hours cell is the strongest numeric association (r=-0.743); age–BPM is only r=0.032, and hours–BPM is r=-0.001.
interpretation: The heatmap therefore highlights an age/listening-duration relationship, while BPM has almost no linear correlation with either variable in this dataset.

title: Bivar Age Vs Listening Time

interpretation: Late-night listening is both the largest group (501 records) and younger by median age than afternoon listening (median 26). This pattern is descriptive, not causal.

title: Bivar Age Vs Listening Setting
